generic.Defined scope/population: Every important business service on the approved register that requires an impact tolerance.
generic.In-scope period: The current resilience register version through to the next scheduled annual review.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each tolerance states a maximum outage duration and a customer volume or value limit.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Tolerance record count equals the important business service count on the register.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Alignment decisions saved in the GRC resilience register with version and decision date.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Tolerances looser than the BCP recovery time objective logged and tightened or justified.
generic.Test population: All important business services and their paired BCP recovery time objectives.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: No important business service with a tolerance exceeding its BCP recovery time objective.
generic.Exception handling path: Misaligned tolerances escalate to the Compliance Analyst for supervisory expectation review.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Each tolerance is duration plus severity, harm-tested, and no looser than the BCP objective.
generic.Evidence location: Resilience register entries in the GRC platform with rationale files in SharePoint.

steps.title: Extract the important business service list from the GRC resilience register
sop: Export the approved important business service list from the GRC resilience register.
Record the register version and export date as the working baseline.
Flag any service on the list that has no tolerance recorded against it.
Done when every register service appears on the working list with its tolerance status.
verify: Reconcile the exported service count to the approved register version count.
Pass when the counts reconcile with no service omitted.

steps.title: Express each tolerance as a duration plus a customer volume or value
sop: State a maximum tolerable outage duration in hours or days for each service.
State the volume or value of affected customers that the tolerance permits.
Reject any tolerance expressed only as a qualitative statement.
Done when every service tolerance carries both a duration and a severity measure.
verify: Filter the tolerance set for entries missing a duration or a severity measure.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

steps.title: Cross-check each tolerance against the supervisor's stated resilience expectation
sop: Collect the supervisory resilience expectations that apply to each service type.
Compare each tolerance against the stated expectation for that service.
Record where a tolerance sits outside the supervisory expectation and by how much.
Done when every tolerance has been compared to a supervisory expectation.
verify: List tolerances that exceed the applicable supervisory expectation.
Pass when the list is empty or each entry carries a documented justification.

steps.title: Test each tolerance against the customer-harm scenario
sop: Run the harm scenario for each service covering payment missed, claim unpaid, or cover unavailable.
Identify the elapsed time at which intolerable customer harm first arises.
Tighten the tolerance where harm arises earlier than the proposed duration.
Done when every tolerance has been tested against its harm scenario and adjusted if needed.
verify: Compare each tolerance duration to the harm-onset time recorded in the scenario.
Pass when no tolerance duration exceeds its recorded harm-onset time.

steps.title: Compare each tolerance to the BCP recovery time objective
sop: Retrieve the BCP recovery time objective for each important business service.
Compare the tolerance duration against the recovery time objective for the same service.
Flag every tolerance that is looser than its recovery time objective.
Done when every service has a recorded comparison of tolerance to recovery objective.
verify: List services whose tolerance duration exceeds the BCP recovery time objective.
Pass when the list is empty.

steps.title: Resolve flagged misalignments with the service owner
sop: Take each flagged tolerance to the service owner with the comparison evidence.
Agree either a tightened tolerance or a revised recovery time objective.
Record the agreed change, its rationale, and the owner who agreed it.
Done when every flagged tolerance has an agreed and recorded resolution.
verify: Re-run the tolerance to recovery objective comparison after the changes.
Pass when no misalignment remains without a recorded resolution.

steps.title: Record the alignment decision per service in the resilience register
sop: Enter the aligned tolerance against each service in the GRC resilience register.
Record the harm test result, the recovery objective comparison, and the decision date.
Save the supporting rationale file to the SharePoint resilience site.
Done when every service carries an aligned tolerance and a dated decision in the register.
verify: Open a sample of register entries and check the tolerance, comparison, and decision date.
Pass when sampled entries are complete and match the agreed tolerances.

generic.Defined scope/population: Business unit heads owning important business services plus technology and third-party managers.
generic.In-scope period: From tolerance approval to the acknowledgement deadline for the current register version.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each acknowledgement names the recipient, the services covered, and the delivery owner.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Acknowledgement count equals the count of service owners on the register.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Issued tolerance sets and the published summary retained with version and approval date.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Owners who have not acknowledged logged with a chase record and escalation.
generic.Test population: All service owners and all technology or third-party managers receiving recovery targets.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: No service owner without a recorded acknowledgement naming a delivery owner.
generic.Exception handling path: Missing acknowledgements escalate to the Business Analyst for the resilience committee.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Each recipient acknowledged the tolerance as binding and named a delivery owner.
generic.Evidence location: Acknowledgement log in the GRC platform with the summary published on the SharePoint resilience site.

steps.title: Build the recipient map from the approved resilience register
sop: List each important business service with its accountable business unit head.
List the technology and third-party managers supporting each service.
Record which services each recipient owns so distribution can be tailored.
Done when every service maps to a business owner and a supporting technology manager.
verify: Filter the map for services without a business owner or technology manager.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

steps.title: Prepare tailored tolerance sets per business unit head
sop: Extract from the register only the tolerances for the services each head owns.
Exclude services the recipient does not own so the full register is not circulated.
State the register version and the approval date on each tailored extract.
Done when each business unit head has an extract limited to their own services.
verify: Cross-check each extract against the recipient map for out-of-scope services.
Pass when no extract contains a service the recipient does not own.

steps.title: Derive recovery targets for the supporting systems
sop: Translate each service tolerance into recovery targets for the systems that support it.
Allocate the tolerance across the dependency chain rather than repeating it per system.
Record the derived target against each system with the service it supports.
Done when every supporting system has a derived recovery target.
verify: Check that the summed dependency targets do not exceed the service tolerance.
Pass when no service has dependency targets exceeding its tolerance.

steps.title: Issue tolerance sets and recovery targets to recipients
sop: Send each business unit head their tailored tolerance extract.
Send technology and third-party managers the derived recovery targets for their systems.
State that the tolerance is a binding target and request a named delivery owner.
Done when every recipient on the map has been sent their extract or targets.
verify: Reconcile the send log to the recipient map.
Pass when every mapped recipient has a recorded send with a timestamp.

steps.title: Collect acknowledgements naming a delivery owner
sop: Collect each recipient's acknowledgement that the tolerance is a binding target.
Record the named delivery owner the recipient assigns for each service or system.
Reject acknowledgements that do not name a delivery owner.
Done when each acknowledgement names both the acknowledger and a delivery owner.
verify: Count acknowledgements with a named delivery owner against the recipient count.
Pass when every recipient has acknowledged and named a delivery owner.

steps.title: Publish the tolerance summary to the SharePoint resilience site
sop: Publish the tolerance summary showing service, tolerance, version, and approval date.
Mark the previous published summary superseded so it cannot be mistaken for current.
Set read access for service owners, business continuity, and technology leads.
Done when the current summary is published with its version and approval date visible.
verify: Open the resilience site and check the published version against the approved register.
Pass when the published summary matches the approved register version.

steps.title: Chase and escalate outstanding acknowledgements
sop: List recipients who have not acknowledged by the deadline.
Chase each recipient and record the chase date and response.
Escalate persistent non-response to the resilience committee and log the escalation in GRC.
Done when no recipient remains unacknowledged without a recorded escalation.
verify: Filter the acknowledgement log for recipients without an acknowledgement or escalation.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

generic.Defined scope/population: All services classified important across every live line of business and customer channel.
generic.In-scope period: The current register cycle from candidate inventory to the documented service list.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each entry holds a customer-outcome definition, owner, customers, channels, volumes, and driver.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Documented service count plus recorded exclusions equals the candidate inventory count.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Documented service list saved in the GRC register with version and documentation date.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Every excluded candidate recorded with the reason it was not documented as a service.
generic.Test population: All candidate services from the inventory and all documented important business services.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: No registered service without an accountable owner and a customer-outcome definition.
generic.Exception handling path: Definitions written as internal functions return to the Business Analyst for rewrite.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Each service maps to a regulatory expectation and a customer-harm scenario.
generic.Evidence location: Service definitions in the GRC resilience register with drafts on the SharePoint resilience site.

steps.title: Write each definition as a customer outcome
sop: Express each service as the outcome the customer receives rather than an internal function.
Rewrite any definition that names a department, system, or process step as the service.
Confirm the outcome wording is understandable to a customer without internal knowledge.
Done when every definition states a customer outcome in customer-facing language.
verify: Review each definition for internal function language rather than an outcome.
Pass when no definition names a department, system, or process step as the service.

steps.title: Record customers served, channels, and typical volumes per service
sop: Record the customer segments each service serves.
Record the channels through which customers reach the service.
Record typical transaction or interaction volumes with the period they cover.
Done when every service carries customers, channels, and a dated volume figure.
verify: Filter the service list for entries missing customers, channels, or volumes.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

steps.title: Map each service to a regulatory expectation
sop: Identify the regulatory driver that makes each service subject to resilience oversight.
Record the specific expectation or rule reference against each service.
Flag any service that cannot be tied to a regulatory expectation for reclassification.
Done when every documented service names at least one regulatory expectation.
verify: Count services with a recorded regulatory reference against the documented service count.
Pass when every documented service carries a regulatory reference.

steps.title: Map each service to a customer-harm scenario
sop: Describe the harm a customer suffers if each service is unavailable.
Record the harm type covering financial loss, loss of cover, or detriment to vulnerable customers.
Flag services where no plausible customer harm can be described.
Done when every documented service has at least one described harm scenario.
verify: Filter the service list for entries without a described harm scenario.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

steps.title: Assign an accountable owner to each documented service
sop: Assign a named accountable owner to each documented important business service.
Confirm the owner accepts accountability for resilience of that service.
Record the owner name, role, and acceptance date in the GRC register.
Done when every documented service has a named owner who has accepted accountability.
verify: Filter the register for services without a named owner or an acceptance date.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

steps.title: Reconcile the documented list against the candidate inventory
sop: Compare the documented service list against the candidate inventory entry by entry.
Record for every candidate not documented the reason it was excluded.
Identify any documented service that was not on the candidate inventory and trace its origin.
Done when every candidate is either documented or carries a recorded exclusion reason.
verify: Sum documented services plus recorded exclusions and compare to the candidate count.
Pass when the totals reconcile to the candidate inventory count.

steps.title: Record the documented service list in the GRC resilience register
sop: Enter each documented service with its definition, owner, drivers, and harm scenario.
Set the register version and the documentation date on the entry set.
Save the supporting draft and reconciliation to the SharePoint resilience site.
Done when every documented service is recorded in the register with a version and date.
verify: Compare the register entry count and content to the documented service list.
Pass when the register matches the documented list entry for entry.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every impact tolerance on the resilience register requiring a documented rationale.
generic.In-scope period: The data window used to derive the tolerance timeframes for the current register version.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each rationale states the data source, the harm point, the severity basis, and assumptions.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Rationale record count equals the impact tolerance count on the register.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Rationale files saved in SharePoint with the data extract date and register version.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Tolerances with incomplete rationale logged with an owner and a completion date.
generic.Test population: All recorded impact tolerances and their supporting evidence sources.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: No tolerance record with an empty rationale or a missing evidence source.
generic.Exception handling path: Unsupported rationales route to the Compliance Analyst for challenge before approval.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Each rationale derives the timeframe from evidence and states its limitations and review trigger.
generic.Evidence location: Rationale appendix in SharePoint linked from each GRC resilience register tolerance entry.

steps.title: List every tolerance requiring a rationale from the GRC register
sop: Export the tolerance set from the GRC resilience register with the register version.
Mark each tolerance as having a rationale, a partial rationale, or none.
Record the owner responsible for supplying each missing rationale.
Done when every tolerance has a rationale status and a named owner.
verify: Reconcile the rationale worklist count to the register tolerance count.
Pass when the counts reconcile with no tolerance omitted.

steps.title: Record the data used to set each timeframe
sop: Identify the data behind each timeframe such as complaint volumes, payment cycles, or claim SLAs.
Record the source system, the extract date, and the period the data covers.
Attach or link the extract so the figure can be reproduced.
Done when every timeframe names its data source and extract date.
verify: Sample rationales and re-derive the timeframe from the cited extract.
Pass when the sampled timeframes reproduce from their cited data.

steps.title: State the point at which customer harm becomes intolerable
sop: State the elapsed disruption time at which customer harm becomes intolerable.
Show how the tolerance timeframe was derived from that harm point.
Record any margin applied between the harm point and the tolerance.
Done when every rationale states a harm point and its link to the timeframe.
verify: Compare each tolerance timeframe against the stated harm point.
Pass when no timeframe is set beyond its stated harm point.

steps.title: Document the severity dimension and its basis
sop: State the severity dimension used such as proportion of customers or value at risk.
Record the numeric limit and the data that supports it.
Explain why that dimension is the right measure for the service.
Done when every rationale carries a severity dimension, a limit, and a supporting basis.
verify: Filter rationales for a missing severity dimension, limit, or basis.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

steps.title: Note assumptions, data limitations, and the review trigger
sop: Record the assumptions the rationale depends on.
Record the known data limitations and how they could affect the tolerance.
State the trigger event that would invalidate the rationale and force a review.
Done when every rationale records assumptions, limitations, and a review trigger.
verify: Filter rationales missing assumptions, limitations, or a review trigger.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

steps.title: Challenge rationales that the evidence does not support
sop: Review each rationale against its cited evidence for logical support.
Raise a challenge where the evidence does not carry the stated conclusion.
Record the challenge, the response, and any change made to the tolerance.
Done when every rationale has been reviewed and every challenge has a recorded response.
verify: List open challenges without a recorded response.
Pass when the list is empty.

steps.title: File the rationale appendix and link it from the register
sop: Compile the rationales into the resilience rationale appendix in SharePoint.
Set the appendix version and the register version it supports.
Link the appendix section from each tolerance entry in the GRC register.
Done when every register tolerance entry links to its rationale in the appendix.
verify: Follow a sample of register links to the appendix sections.
Pass when every sampled link resolves to a complete rationale.

generic.Defined scope/population: The draft important business services list plus every excluded candidate and its reason.
generic.In-scope period: The executive engagement window ahead of the Board approval submission.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each challenge record names the raiser, the service, the challenge, and the response.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Challenges recorded in the notes equal the challenges raised at the session.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Session notes retained with attendance, date, and the list version discussed.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Every challenge closed as an agreed change or a recorded reason for no change.
generic.Test population: All contested services and every challenge raised in the executive session.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Notes record each challenge, its response, and the confirmed list version.
generic.Exception handling path: Unresolved challenges route to the Chief Operating Officer before Board submission.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Executive and board position on the final list confirmed before formal approval is requested.
generic.Evidence location: Session notes in SharePoint linked to the register version in the GRC platform.

steps.title: Assemble the draft list, criteria, and exclusions for circulation
sop: Compile the draft services list with the inclusion criteria applied to each service.
Attach the excluded candidate list with the reason recorded for each exclusion.
Set the list version and the date on the pack cover.
Done when the pack holds the draft list, the criteria, and the exclusion reasons.
verify: Check the pack against the classification output for missing services or exclusions.
Pass when every classified candidate appears as included or excluded in the pack.

steps.title: Circulate the pack ahead of the executive session
sop: Send the pack to executive attendees with enough lead time to review it.
State the decision being sought and the questions on which input is needed.
Record the circulation date and the recipient list in SharePoint.
Done when every executive attendee has received the pack ahead of the session.
verify: Reconcile the circulation list to the executive attendee list.
Pass when every attendee received the pack before the session date.

steps.title: Walk the committee through the most contested services
sop: Identify the services whose classification was borderline or disputed.
Present the basis for each classification with the criteria scores behind it.
Invite challenge on each contested service before moving to the next.
Done when every contested service has been presented and opened to challenge.
verify: Compare the services presented against the borderline list from classification.
Pass when every borderline service was presented to the committee.

steps.title: Capture each challenge raised with its response
sop: Record every challenge with the raiser, the service, and the point made.
Record either the agreed change or the reason no change was made.
Assign an owner and a date to any challenge needing further work.
Done when every challenge raised has a recorded response or a follow-up owner.
verify: Count recorded challenges against the challenges heard in the session.
Pass when every challenge heard is recorded with a response.

steps.title: Update the draft list from the agreed changes
sop: Apply each agreed change to the draft services list.
Increment the list version and record what changed against the previous version.
Re-check that every added or removed service still satisfies the inclusion criteria.
Done when the updated list reflects every agreed change with a new version number.
verify: Compare the updated list to the challenge log for unapplied agreed changes.
Pass when every agreed change is reflected in the updated list.

steps.title: Confirm the executive position on the final list
sop: Present the updated list version to the executive attendees for confirmation.
Take an explicit position from each executive on the final list.
Record any residual disagreement and how it will be handled at Board.
Done when the executive position on the final list version is recorded.
verify: Check the notes for a recorded position from each executive attendee.
Pass when every attendee has a recorded position on the final list.

steps.title: File the session notes and link the confirmed list version in GRC
sop: Write the notes covering attendance, challenges, responses, and the confirmed version.
File the notes in SharePoint with the session date and the list version.
Link the notes to the register version entry in the GRC platform.
Done when the filed notes are linked to the confirmed register version in GRC.
verify: Follow the GRC link and check the notes show challenges, responses, and the version.
Pass when the link resolves and the notes carry all three elements.

generic.Defined scope/population: The final important business services list and every associated impact tolerance.
generic.In-scope period: From Board paper submission to the recorded approval effective date.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Register carries the approved version, approval date, minute reference, and effective date.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Tolerances approved in the minute equal the tolerance count in the submitted paper.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Board paper, rationale appendix, and minute extract retained with version and date.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Every Board condition logged as a tracked action with an owner and a due date.
generic.Test population: All services and tolerances submitted for Board approval.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Board approval date, minute reference, and approved version recorded in the register.
generic.Exception handling path: Minutes approving the paper but not the tolerances return for correction before recording.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: The minute records approval of the list and of each impact tolerance specifically.
generic.Evidence location: Board minute extract in SharePoint with the approved version recorded in the GRC register.

steps.title: Assemble the Board paper with the rationale appendix
sop: Compile the final services list and the tolerance set into the Board paper.
Attach the rationale appendix supporting each tolerance.
State explicitly that approval is sought for the list and for each tolerance.
Done when the paper holds the list, the tolerances, and the rationale appendix.
verify: Reconcile the paper's service and tolerance counts to the confirmed register version.
Pass when both counts reconcile to the confirmed version.

steps.title: Obtain second-line review before submission
sop: Review the paper for regulatory completeness and consistency with the register.
Record any correction required and confirm it is made before submission.
Record the second-line review sign-off with the reviewer name and date.
Done when the paper carries a dated second-line review sign-off.
verify: Check the paper for a second-line sign-off and closed review comments.
Pass when the sign-off is present and no review comment remains open.

steps.title: Submit the paper to the Board
sop: Submit the paper into the Board pack ahead of the submission deadline.
Confirm the agenda item states approval of the list and the tolerances.
Record the submission date and the meeting date in SharePoint.
Done when the paper is on the Board agenda as an approval item.
verify: Check the published Board agenda for the item and its approval framing.
Pass when the item appears as an approval item for the list and tolerances.

steps.title: Confirm the minute records approval of the list and each tolerance
sop: Read the draft minute for the specific approvals granted.
Confirm it records approval of the services list and of each impact tolerance.
Request a minute correction where only the paper is recorded as approved.
Done when the final minute records approval of both the list and the tolerances.
verify: Check the final minute wording against the approval sought in the paper.
Pass when the minute records approval of the list and of each tolerance.

steps.title: Record the approved version and effective date in the resilience register
sop: Enter the approved register version, approval date, and minute reference in GRC.
Set the effective date from which the approved list and tolerances apply.
Mark the previous approved version superseded in the register.
Done when the register shows the approved version, date, minute reference, and effective date.
verify: Open the register entry and check all four recorded values against the minute.
Pass when all four values are present and match the minute.

steps.title: Log Board conditions and follow-ups as tracked actions
sop: Extract every condition or requested follow-up from the Board minute.
Raise a tracked action in the GRC platform for each one.
Assign an owner and a due date to every action and link it to the register version.
Done when every Board condition has a tracked action with an owner and due date.
verify: Reconcile tracked action count to conditions recorded in the minute.
Pass when the counts reconcile and no action is missing an owner or date.

steps.title: File the minute extract with the approved paper
sop: Obtain the approved minute extract for the resilience agenda item.
File it in SharePoint alongside the submitted paper and rationale appendix.
Link the filed extract from the approved register version entry in GRC.
Done when the minute extract is filed and linked from the register.
verify: Follow the register link and confirm it opens the minute extract.
Pass when the link resolves and the extract shows the approval date and reference.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every register entry covering service definitions, owners, tolerances, and retired services.
generic.In-scope period: The twelve months since the last review plus any material change since that date.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each entry carries a review date, reviewer, validity confirmation, and next review date.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Reviewed entry count plus retirements equals the prior register entry count plus additions.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Refreshed register saved with the new version, review date, and change log.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Entries that could not be reviewed logged with an owner and a completion date.
generic.Test population: All register entries plus material change candidates since the last review.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: No register entry with a review date older than twelve months.
generic.Exception handling path: Unreviewed entries escalate to the Compliance Analyst before the register version is issued.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Each definition, owner, and tolerance confirmed valid or re-baselined with a next review date.
generic.Evidence location: Refreshed register in the GRC platform with the change log on the SharePoint resilience site.

steps.title: Open the annual review against the current register version
sop: Export the current approved register version with each entry's last review date.
Flag every entry whose review date is approaching or beyond twelve months.
Assign a reviewer to each entry and set the review completion date.
Done when every register entry has an assigned reviewer and a review due date.
verify: Reconcile the review worklist count to the register entry count.
Pass when every register entry appears once on the worklist.

steps.title: Confirm each service definition, owner, and tolerance is still valid
sop: Review each service definition against how the service actually operates today.
Confirm the named owner still holds accountability for the service.
Confirm the tolerance still reflects the current duration and severity position.
Done when every entry carries a validity confirmation or a recorded change.
verify: Filter the worklist for entries without a validity confirmation or change.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

steps.title: Assess material changes since the last review for new candidates
sop: List material changes since the last review such as new products, outsourcing, or acquisitions.
Assess each change for services that should now be candidates.
Add new candidates to the inventory and route them through classification.
Done when every material change has been assessed for new candidate services.
verify: Compare the change list against product, sourcing, and system change records.
Pass when no recorded material change is absent from the assessment.

steps.title: Retire services no longer offered
sop: Identify register services that are no longer offered to customers.
Record the retirement rationale and the date the service ceased.
Mark the entry retired in the GRC register rather than deleting it.
Done when every ceased service is marked retired with a rationale and date.
verify: Filter retired entries for a missing rationale or retirement date.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

steps.title: Re-baseline tolerances where volumes or channels have shifted
sop: Compare current volumes, channels, and customer profiles against the tolerance basis.
Re-derive the tolerance where the shift is material enough to change the harm point.
Record the re-baselined tolerance with its updated rationale and evidence.
Done when every materially shifted service has a re-baselined tolerance and rationale.
verify: Check re-baselined tolerances against the updated rationale evidence.
Pass when every re-baselined tolerance has supporting updated evidence.

steps.title: Set the next review date and off-cycle refresh triggers
sop: Set the next scheduled review date on every active register entry.
Record the trigger events that force an off-cycle refresh before that date.
Confirm the triggers are monitored by a named owner.
Done when every active entry has a next review date and recorded triggers.
verify: Filter active entries for a missing next review date or trigger set.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

steps.title: Issue the refreshed register version with a change log
sop: Increment the register version and record the review completion date.
Write the change log listing additions, retirements, and re-baselined tolerances.
Publish the change log to the SharePoint resilience site with the new version.
Done when the refreshed version is issued with a published change log.
verify: Query the refreshed register for entries with a review date older than twelve months.
Pass when the query returns no such entry.

generic.Defined scope/population: The approved services, tolerances, and approval dates required by the supervisory return.
generic.In-scope period: The reporting period the supervisory return covers up to its submission deadline.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Return carries every prescribed field including service, tolerance, and approval date.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Figures in the return reconcile to the approved register version, not to drafts.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Submitted return, receipt, and reference number retained with the submission timestamp.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Reconciliation differences logged and resolved before the return is signed off.
generic.Test population: Every service and tolerance the supervisory return requires to be reported.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Submission logged with a receipt reference and a next due date recorded.
generic.Exception handling path: Unreconciled figures block submission and return to the Business Analyst for correction.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Second-line reviewed return submitted in the prescribed format by the supervisory deadline.
generic.Evidence location: Submission receipt in the GRC regulatory filing inventory with the return filed in SharePoint.

steps.title: Confirm the prescribed return format and deadline
sop: Obtain the supervisor's prescribed format and field definitions for the resilience return.
Record the submission deadline and the reporting period the return covers.
Note any change from the previous return format and its impact on the data.
Done when the format, field list, and deadline are recorded for this submission.
verify: Compare the recorded field list against the supervisor's current template.
Pass when the field list matches the current supervisory template.

steps.title: Extract the approved register version for the return
sop: Extract services, tolerances, and approval dates from the approved GRC register version.
Exclude any draft or unapproved entry from the extract.
Record the register version and the extract timestamp on the working file.
Done when the extract is taken from the approved version and version-stamped.
verify: Check the extract version against the Board-approved register version.
Pass when the extract cites the approved version and no draft entries appear.

steps.title: Populate the return in the prescribed format
sop: Map each extract field into the prescribed return field.
Populate every mandatory field and record why any optional field is left blank.
Apply the supervisor's stated formats for dates, durations, and volumes.
Done when every mandatory field in the return is populated.
verify: Run the format validation for missing or malformed mandatory fields.
Pass when validation returns no missing or malformed mandatory field.

steps.title: Reconcile every figure in the return to the approved register
sop: Compare each reported service and tolerance back to the approved register entry.
Investigate and resolve any difference before the return is finalised.
Record the reconciliation with the register version it was performed against.
Done when every reported figure ties to an approved register entry.
verify: Count reconciled return rows against the approved register entry count.
Pass when the counts reconcile and no unexplained difference remains.

steps.title: Obtain second-line compliance sign-off before submission
sop: Present the return, the reconciliation, and the register version to second-line review.
Record every review comment and confirm it is resolved before sign-off.
Record the sign-off with the reviewer name and date.
Done when the return carries a dated second-line sign-off with no open comments.
verify: Check the sign-off record and the review comment log.
Pass when the sign-off is present and no comment remains open.

steps.title: Submit by the deadline and retain the receipt
sop: Submit the signed return through the supervisor's prescribed channel.
Capture the submission receipt, the reference number, and the timestamp.
File the submitted return and the receipt in the SharePoint regulatory folder.
Done when the return is submitted and the receipt reference is captured.
verify: Check the submission timestamp against the supervisory deadline.
Pass when the submission timestamp precedes the deadline and a receipt is held.

steps.title: Log the submission in the regulatory filing inventory
sop: Create the filing inventory entry in the GRC platform for this submission.
Record the receipt reference, the submission date, and the register version reported.
Set the next due date and the owner responsible for the next return.
Done when the inventory entry holds the receipt reference and the next due date.
verify: Open the inventory entry and check the reference, submission date, and next due date.
Pass when all three are recorded and the next due date is in the future.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every important business service definition requiring an accountable executive signature.
generic.In-scope period: From routing for signature to the publication deadline for the definition set.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each sign-off records the signer name, role, date, and the document version signed.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Signed definition count equals the definition count routed for signature.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Signed definitions retained in SharePoint with version and signature date.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Unsigned definitions logged with a chase record and an escalation to the function head.
generic.Test population: All service definitions in the final set awaiting executive approval.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: No service definition without a dated executive signature before publication.
generic.Exception handling path: Definitions unsigned five working days before publication escalate to the Chief Operating Officer.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Each executive signed the specific definition and owner assignment, not a summary list.
generic.Evidence location: Signed definition set in SharePoint with the sign-off tracker in Confluence.

steps.title: Map each definition to its accountable executive
sop: List each service definition with the executive accountable for that service.
Confirm the accountability with the executive's office before routing.
Record the mapping in the Confluence sign-off tracker.
Done when every definition maps to one named accountable executive.
verify: Filter the tracker for definitions without a named accountable executive.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

steps.title: Route each definition individually for signature
sop: Send each executive the specific definitions they own rather than the full set.
Include the owner assignment and the definition version in each routing.
State the signature deadline and how to return the signed definition.
Done when every definition has been routed to its accountable executive.
verify: Reconcile routed definitions to the tracker mapping.
Pass when every mapped definition has a recorded routing date.

steps.title: Confirm each signature is against the specific definition
sop: Check each returned signature names the specific service definition signed.
Reject signatures given only against a summary list or covering note.
Confirm the owner assignment on the signed definition matches the register.
Done when every accepted signature is against a named service definition.
verify: Sample signed definitions for the service name and owner assignment on the signed page.
Pass when every sampled signature names the specific definition and owner.

steps.title: Record signer name, role, date, and version against each definition
sop: Record the signer name and role against each signed definition in the tracker.
Record the signature date and the document version that was signed.
Reject any signature returned against a superseded version.
Done when every signed definition carries a name, role, date, and version.
verify: Filter the tracker for signed rows missing a name, role, date, or version.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

steps.title: Chase definitions still unsigned as the deadline approaches
sop: List definitions still unsigned five working days before publication.
Chase each accountable executive directly and record the chase date.
Escalate to the Chief Operating Officer where no signature follows the chase.
Done when every unsigned definition has a recorded chase and escalation.
verify: Filter unsigned definitions for a missing chase or escalation record.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

steps.title: File the signed definition set in SharePoint
sop: File each signed definition in the SharePoint resilience record set.
Set the version and signature date properties on each filed document.
Link each filed document from its row in the Confluence tracker.
Done when every signed definition is filed and linked from the tracker.
verify: Follow a sample of tracker links to the filed signed definitions.
Pass when every sampled link resolves to a signed and dated definition.

steps.title: Confirm the full set is signed before releasing for publication
sop: Review the tracker for any definition still without an accepted signature.
Decide whether to hold publication or publish a reduced set with the gap recorded.
Record the release decision and the date it was taken.
Done when the release decision is recorded against the complete tracker.
verify: Count signed definitions against the routed definition count.
Pass when the counts match or the gap carries a recorded release decision.

generic.Defined scope/population: The Board-approved important business service definitions due for publication.
generic.In-scope period: From the approval effective date to the next approved register version.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each published definition shows its version, approval date, and accountable owner.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Published definition count equals the Board-approved register entry count.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Published set retained with version and approval date, prior versions archived.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Publication differences from the approved register logged and corrected before notification.
generic.Test population: All approved definitions and every previously published version of the set.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Current approved version published with the approval date and prior versions archived.
generic.Exception handling path: Mismatches against the approved register route to the Business Analyst before notification.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Published set matches the Board-approved register entry by entry with owners notified.
generic.Evidence location: Published definitions on the SharePoint resilience site with the archive in Confluence.

steps.title: Take the Board-approved definition set as the publication baseline
sop: Extract the approved definitions from the register version cited in the Board minute.
Confirm no unapproved edit has been made since the approval date.
Record the baseline version and approval date for the publication.
Done when the publication baseline is fixed to the approved register version.
verify: Compare the baseline version against the version in the Board minute.
Pass when the two versions are identical.

steps.title: Publish the definitions to the SharePoint resilience site
sop: Publish each approved definition to the resilience site with its accountable owner.
Show the version number and the approval date on the published page.
Set read access for service owners, business continuity, and technology leads.
Done when every approved definition is published with version and approval date visible.
verify: Open the resilience site and count published definitions against the baseline.
Pass when the published count equals the baseline count.

steps.title: Archive the previous version and mark it superseded
sop: Move the previous published definition set into the Confluence archive space.
Mark it superseded with a link forward to the current published version.
Remove the previous version from any location browsed as the current set.
Done when no earlier version is reachable without a superseded marking.
verify: Search the resilience site and Confluence for unmarked earlier versions.
Pass when only the current version returns as current.

steps.title: Reconcile the published set to the approved register entry by entry
sop: Compare each published definition against its GRC register entry.
Check the definition wording, the accountable owner, and the version on both.
Correct any difference on the published page before notifying stakeholders.
Done when every published definition matches its approved register entry.
verify: List published definitions differing from the register in wording, owner, or version.
Pass when the list is empty.

steps.title: Notify service owners, business continuity, and technology leads
sop: Send the publication notice to service owners, business continuity, and technology leads.
State that the new baseline is live and give the published location and version.
State what changed from the previous baseline for each audience.
Done when every audience group has been sent the publication notice.
verify: Reconcile the notification list to the service owner and dependency lead lists.
Pass when every service owner and technology lead has a recorded notification.

steps.title: Confirm stakeholders can reach the published definitions
sop: Ask a sample of service owners and technology leads to open the published set.
Record any access failure and raise the permission request needed.
Re-check access after each permission change.
Done when every sampled stakeholder can open the published definitions.
verify: Check outstanding access requests against the resilience site permission list.
Pass when no stakeholder group is left without read access.

steps.title: Record the publication against the register version in GRC
sop: Record the publication date and location against the approved register version.
Link the published location from the register entry.
Note the archive location of the superseded version on the same entry.
Done when the register entry records the publication date, location, and archive.
verify: Follow the register link to the published set and to the archive.
Pass when both links resolve to the correct versions.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every important business service on the register requiring a tolerance threshold.
generic.In-scope period: From threshold definition to the effective date recorded against each service.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each threshold holds a numeric duration, a severity limit, and an effective date.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Threshold record count equals the important business service count on the register.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Threshold entries stored in the GRC register with effective date and version.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Thresholds that cannot be measured from existing data logged with a measurement plan.
generic.Test population: All important business services and the operational data supporting their thresholds.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: No important business service without a numeric duration and severity threshold.
generic.Exception handling path: Unmeasurable thresholds escalate to the Chief Operating Officer for revision or instrumentation.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Each threshold is measurable from existing data and carries a breach escalation trigger.
generic.Evidence location: Threshold entries in the GRC resilience register with measurability evidence in the BI platform.

steps.title: Set a maximum tolerable disruption duration per service
sop: Set the maximum tolerable disruption duration in hours or days for each service.
Base the duration on the harm point established for that service.
Reject any duration expressed as a range without an upper bound.
Done when every important business service has a single numeric duration.
verify: Filter the threshold set for services without a numeric duration.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

steps.title: Define the severity measure and its numeric limit
sop: Choose the severity measure such as customers affected, transactions failed, or value delayed.
Set a numeric limit for that measure per service.
Record why that measure is the right one for the service.
Done when every service carries a severity measure with a numeric limit.
verify: Filter the threshold set for services without a severity measure or limit.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

steps.title: Confirm each threshold is measurable from existing operational data
sop: Identify the operational data source that would evidence each threshold in a disruption.
Build or locate the BI query that returns the duration and severity measure.
Flag thresholds that cannot be measured from existing data before agreeing them.
Done when every threshold has a confirmed data source or a raised measurability flag.
verify: Run the BI query for a sample of thresholds against recent operational data.
Pass when each sampled query returns the duration and severity measure.

steps.title: Resolve thresholds that cannot be measured
sop: List thresholds flagged as not measurable from existing data.
Agree either a revised measure or an instrumentation change with an owner and date.
Record the resolution against the threshold in the register.
Done when every flagged threshold has an agreed and recorded resolution.
verify: Filter flagged thresholds for entries without a resolution owner and date.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

steps.title: Define the breach escalation trigger and notification path
sop: Define the point during a disruption at which a threshold breach is declared.
Name who must be notified on breach and the timeframe for that notification.
Confirm the notification path aligns with the incident management process.
Done when every threshold carries a breach trigger, a notified party, and a timeframe.
verify: Filter thresholds for a missing trigger, notified party, or notification timeframe.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

steps.title: Enter each threshold into the GRC resilience register
sop: Enter the duration, severity limit, and breach trigger against each service in GRC.
Set the effective date from which the threshold applies.
Link the measurability evidence from the BI platform to the register entry.
Done when every service carries a complete threshold entry with an effective date.
verify: Reconcile register threshold entries to the important business service count.
Pass when every service has one complete threshold entry.

steps.title: Review the threshold set with the accountable executive
sop: Review the full threshold set for consistency across comparable services.
Challenge thresholds that look inconsistent with the harm evidence.
Record acceptance of the threshold set with the review date.
Done when the threshold set carries a dated executive acceptance.
verify: Check the register for the recorded acceptance and its date.
Pass when the acceptance is recorded against the current threshold version.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every candidate service on the inventory awaiting an importance classification.
generic.In-scope period: The classification cycle for the current candidate inventory version.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each candidate carries harm scores, market-impact scores, an outcome, and a reason.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Classified candidate count equals the candidate inventory count.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Scored classification saved in the GRC register with version and classification date.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Every not-important outcome recorded with the reason so exclusions can be challenged.
generic.Test population: All candidate services on the inventory including borderline cases.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: No candidate service left unclassified or classified without a recorded reason.
generic.Exception handling path: Borderline classifications route to the Compliance Analyst as second reviewer.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Every candidate scored on both criteria sets with the agreed threshold applied.
generic.Evidence location: Scored classification sheet in the GRC platform with working papers in SharePoint.

steps.title: Confirm the classification criteria and threshold
sop: Confirm the customer-harm criteria covering financial loss, loss of cover, and vulnerable impact.
Confirm the market-impact criteria covering volume, market share, concentration, and substitutability.
Confirm the score threshold that marks a candidate important.
Done when the criteria sets and the threshold are recorded for this classification cycle.
verify: Compare the criteria and threshold against the approved classification methodology.
Pass when both match the approved methodology or the change is documented.

steps.title: Score each candidate against the customer-harm criteria
sop: Score every candidate for financial loss, loss of cover, and vulnerable-customer impact.
Record the evidence behind each score rather than a bare number.
Leave no candidate unscored on any harm criterion.
Done when every candidate carries a score on each customer-harm criterion.
verify: Filter the sheet for candidates with a blank customer-harm score.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

steps.title: Score each candidate against the market-impact criteria
sop: Score every candidate for volume, market share, concentration, and substitutability.
Use distribution and market data rather than judgement alone where data exists.
Record the data source behind each market-impact score.
Done when every candidate carries a score on each market-impact criterion.
verify: Filter the sheet for candidates with a blank market-impact score.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

steps.title: Apply the threshold to mark each candidate important or not important
sop: Apply the agreed threshold to the combined scores for each candidate.
Mark each candidate important or not important with no candidate left unresolved.
Flag candidates falling within the borderline band around the threshold.
Done when every candidate carries an importance outcome and any borderline flag.
verify: Count classified candidates against the candidate inventory count.
Pass when the counts reconcile with no candidate unclassified.

steps.title: Record the reason for every not-important outcome
sop: Write the reason each not-important candidate fell below the threshold.
Reference the specific criteria scores that drove the outcome.
Record the reason so the exclusion can be challenged later.
Done when every not-important candidate has a recorded reason.
verify: Filter not-important candidates for a missing reason.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

steps.title: Second-review the borderline classifications
sop: Review every candidate flagged borderline against its scores and evidence.
Confirm or change the outcome and record the reviewer name and date.
Escalate any classification the reviewer and preparer cannot agree.
Done when every borderline candidate has a second-reviewer decision recorded.
verify: Filter borderline candidates for a missing second-reviewer decision.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

steps.title: Record the classification outcome in the GRC register
sop: Enter each candidate outcome, its scores, and its reason into the GRC register.
Set the classification version and date on the entry set.
File the scoring working papers on the SharePoint resilience site.
Done when every candidate outcome is recorded in the register with a version and date.
verify: Compare register entries against the scoring sheet outcome by outcome.
Pass when the register matches the scoring sheet for every candidate.

generic.Defined scope/population: All customer-facing services across every live line of business and customer journey.
generic.In-scope period: The product and process catalogue as at the inventory extract date.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each candidate carries an owner, a line of business, and a customer channel.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Candidate count plus recorded drops equals the extracted catalogue entry count.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Candidate inventory saved in SharePoint with the extract date and version.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Every dropped internal function recorded with the reason it was not a candidate.
generic.Test population: All live lines of business and all customer journeys in the process model.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: No live line of business absent from the candidate inventory.
generic.Exception handling path: Gaps raised by business owners route to the Business Analyst for inventory addition.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Business owners confirmed no customer-facing service they run is missing.
generic.Evidence location: Candidate inventory in the SharePoint resilience site with source extracts attached.

steps.title: Extract the candidate list from the product catalogue and process model
sop: Extract every product from the catalogue covering all live lines of business.
Extract the process model entries that deliver those products to customers.
Record the extract date and source for each row.
Done when the extract covers every live line of business with a dated source.
verify: Compare the lines of business in the extract to the live product register.
Pass when every live line of business appears in the extract.

steps.title: Add customer journeys as candidate services
sop: Add the new business, renewal, claims, complaints, and payment journeys as candidates.
Split a journey where it differs materially by line of business or channel.
Record the journey stages that make each candidate a distinct customer outcome.
Done when every customer journey appears as at least one candidate service.
verify: Check each named journey appears at least once on the candidate list.
Pass when no named journey is absent from the list.

steps.title: Cross-check the policy administration system for live product coverage
sop: Query the policy administration system for products with in-force policies.
Compare that list against the catalogue extract for products not represented.
Add any in-force product missing from the extract as a candidate.
Done when every in-force product is represented on the candidate list.
verify: List in-force products from policy admin absent from the candidate list.
Pass when the list is empty.

steps.title: Record owner, line of business, and channel per candidate
sop: Record the accountable owner for each candidate service.
Record the line of business and the customer channels it is delivered through.
Use warehouse volume data to record indicative volumes per candidate.
Done when every candidate has an owner, a line of business, and a channel.
verify: Filter the candidate list for rows missing an owner, line of business, or channel.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

steps.title: Drop internal functions that are not customer-facing outcomes
sop: Identify candidates that describe an internal function rather than a customer outcome.
Record the reason each is dropped rather than deleting the row.
Retain the dropped list so the decision can be challenged.
Done when every dropped candidate carries a recorded reason.
verify: Sum retained candidates plus dropped rows and compare to the extracted count.
Pass when the totals reconcile to the extracted count.

steps.title: Confirm completeness with each business owner
sop: Send each business owner the candidates recorded for their area.
Ask each owner to confirm no customer-facing service they run is missing.
Add any service the owner names and record who raised it.
Done when every business owner has confirmed completeness for their area.
verify: Reconcile received confirmations to the business owner list.
Pass when every business owner has confirmed or has a recorded escalation.

steps.title: Publish the candidate inventory version to SharePoint
sop: Compile the confirmed candidates and the dropped list into the inventory version.
Attach the catalogue, warehouse, and policy admin extracts as sources.
Publish the version to the SharePoint resilience site with the extract date.
Done when the versioned inventory is published with its source extracts attached.
verify: Open the published inventory and check the version, date, and attached extracts.
Pass when all three are present and the line-of-business coverage is complete.

generic.Defined scope/population: The people, process, technology, facility, data, and third-party resources per important service.
generic.In-scope period: The current approved register version through to the next resource mapping refresh.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each dependency records its type, owner, criticality, and CMDB reference where applicable.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Mapped application dependencies reconcile one to one with CMDB configuration items.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Resource maps saved with version and mapping date in the GRC platform.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Dependencies with no CMDB record raised as a gap with an owner and a due date.
generic.Test population: All important business services and every dependency in their end-to-end chains.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: No mapped application dependency missing a CMDB configuration item.
generic.Exception handling path: CMDB gaps route to the Business Analyst for registration before the map is baselined.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: End-to-end chain mapped with single points of failure and shared resources flagged.
generic.Evidence location: Resource maps in the GRC platform with CMDB reconciliation evidence in SharePoint.

steps.title: Map people, process, technology, facility, data, and third-party dependencies
sop: For each important business service list the dependencies in all six resource categories.
Record the owner and the criticality of each dependency to the service.
Leave no resource category unaddressed even where the answer is none.
Done when every service has dependencies recorded across all six categories.
verify: Filter the map for services with an unaddressed resource category.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

steps.title: Trace applications end to end from customer entry to settlement
sop: Trace the application chain from the customer entry point through to settlement.
Include the interfaces and batch jobs that move data between applications.
Record the sequence so a break can be located to a specific hop.
Done when every service has an unbroken application chain from entry to settlement.
verify: Walk each chain for hops with no upstream or downstream connection recorded.
Pass when every chain runs unbroken from entry point to settlement.

steps.title: Identify third parties and intra-group providers in the chain
sop: Identify every third party and intra-group provider in each service chain.
Record the contract reference and the exit arrangement for each provider.
Flag providers with no documented exit arrangement.
Done when every provider in a chain has a contract reference and exit position.
verify: Filter the provider list for a missing contract reference or exit arrangement.
Pass when the filtered list is empty or each gap carries an owner.

steps.title: Flag single points of failure and shared resources
sop: Identify dependencies with no alternative path within the tolerance window.
Identify resources shared across more than one important business service.
Flag each on the map with the services it affects.
Done when every single point of failure and shared resource is flagged.
verify: Cross-check the shared resource flags against dependency appearances across services.
Pass when every dependency appearing in more than one service is flagged as shared.

steps.title: Reconcile mapped applications to CMDB configuration items
sop: Look up each mapped application, interface, and batch job in the CMDB.
Record the configuration item reference against the dependency on the map.
List every dependency with no matching configuration item.
Done when every mapped application dependency has a CMDB reference or a gap entry.
verify: Count dependencies with a CMDB reference against total mapped application dependencies.
Pass when every mapped application dependency carries a CMDB reference.

steps.title: Raise CMDB registration gaps with owners and due dates
sop: Raise a gap record for each dependency with no CMDB configuration item.
Assign an owner and a due date for registering the item.
Re-reconcile the map after each registration is confirmed.
Done when every CMDB gap is closed or carries an owner and a due date.
verify: Filter open CMDB gaps for entries without an owner or due date.
Pass when the filtered list is empty.

steps.title: Baseline the resource maps in the GRC platform
sop: Load each completed resource map against its service in the GRC platform.
Set the map version and the mapping date on each entry.
File the CMDB reconciliation evidence on the SharePoint resilience site.
Done when every important business service carries a versioned baselined map.
verify: Count baselined maps against the important business service count in the register.
Pass when every service has one baselined and dated resource map.
